transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

Probably not. A loud hum or buzz from an induction hob on maximum power is commonly normal, particularly with a large, heavy or multi-layer stockpot: the magnetic field can make the pan base vibrate. It is more likely to be the cookware than the hob if it is only this pot and the sound eases when the power is reduced. Try the same zone with another flat, magnetic pan, and also reduce the setting by two levels. If the noise happens with several pans, becomes a harsh crackling sound, or is accompanied by a burning smell, sparks, or the hob cutting out/showing a code, stop using it and arrange an engineer visit.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I tried it with my heavy cast iron pot and that's quiet, but a cheap frying pan is noisy too. It's also much quieter at 6 and below. No codes or cutting out, and no burning smell. Does that sound like it's just the pans?

Yes — that pattern points to the pans, not the hob. The quiet cast-iron pot is a useful comparison: it is rigid and tends not to resonate, whereas thinner, cheaper or multi-layer bases can vibrate audibly when the hob is delivering maximum power. Use the noisy pans at a lower setting if the sound is bothersome; it is not in itself a sign the hob is about to fail. With the pans cold and the hob off, check whether the noisy pan bases are flat and not bowed, loose or separating—those features make the buzz more likely. Stop using the hob and seek repair only if it develops harsh cracking, sparks, a burning smell, error codes or starts cutting out.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
The new stockpot has a sandwich base, maybe slightly smaller than the ring. Could that be part of why it buzzes?

[Heading: Likely cause: pan misuse / blocked vents / airflow]
Yes. A sandwich base can be more prone to humming because its bonded layers can resonate under high induction power. A pot that is slightly smaller than the marked ring can also make the sound more noticeable, although it should still work normally if the base is flat, magnetic and the hob detects it reliably. The quiet cast-iron pot and the big reduction in noise at level 6 or below strongly support this being cookware resonance rather than the hob failing. I cannot confirm the exact recommended pan-base range for PUE611BB1E from the model reference alone, so check Bosch’s manual/support pages if you want the specified zone and pan sizes; otherwise, use that pot on a lower setting or choose a heavier, rigid-based pot. An engineer is only warranted if the noise changes to harsh crackling or comes with a smell, sparks, errors or shut-downs.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
